This is a suit filed by the plaintiff for the relief of perpetual injunction to restrain the defendants,
their men, agents, servants or anybody claiming through them from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the plaintiff over the suit schedule property and for such other and favourable reliefs.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the plaintiff is that, the suit schedule site bearing No.2161-A, formed in Sy.No.3/2 vide Conversion Order No.ALN(N)SR/92/03-04, dated 25.10.2003 issued by the Special Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Bangalore District, situated at Gidadhakonenahalli Village, Yeshwanthapura Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk, measuring East to West: 40 feet and North to South: 30 feet was alloted in favour of one Smt.Savitha Muniraju by The Karnataka State 'D'
Group Employees Central Association.

sentences.text: The Possession Certificate was issued in her favour on 30.11.2004.
On 28.11.2004, the President of the said Society executed a Registered Sale Deed in her favour.
Then Khatha came to be changed in her name and she was in possession and enjoyment of the suit property.
Since there were some typographical error in her Sale Deed, the Registered Rectification Deed came to be executed on 17.10.2019.
Then she constructed a small shed in the suit schedule property and obtained the electricity connection.

On 12.03.2020, she sold the suit schedule property in favour of plaintiff under a Registered Sale Deed and by virtue of the said Sale Deed, the plaintiff was put in possession of the suit schedule property and power supply came to be changed in his name.
Then Uttara Pathra, Khatha Certificate, Khatha Extract and other revenue records came to be changed in the name of plaintiff.
The change of ownership was intimated to the BESCOM for changing the consumer name.

Though the defendants have no manner of right, title or interest over Chandrashekar K N vs Prathap Kumar on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58143715/
2 the suit schedule property, on 25.02.2021, they made an illegal attempt to demolish the shed existing in the suit schedule property.

sentences.text: On enquiry, the plaintiff came to know that, the defendants are engaged in real estate business and having an eagle eye over the vacant sites.
With an intention of blackmailing the plaintiff, the defendants have threatened him with dire consequences.
The plaintiff has resisted their act with the help of his family members ad friends and also approached the jurisdictional police.
But the police did not take any action, as the matter is civil in nature.
Hence he was constrained to file this suit for the aforementioned reliefs.
3. Inspite of service of suit summons, the defendant No.1 remained absent and placed him exparte.
The defendant No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed his written statement and denied each and every contentions taken in the plaint.

Further contended that, the written statement schedule vacant site bearing No.2163 (Corner Site), formed in Sy.No.3/2, vide Conversion Order No.ALN/(N)SR/92-2003-2004 dated 25.10.2003 issued by the Special Deputy Commissioner,
Bangalore District, situated at Gidadhakonenahalli Village, Yeshwanthapura Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk, measuring East to West: 30 feet and North to South: 40 feet was allotted in favour of one A.Ramakrishna Shetty, who was the member of the Society.
The Society executed a Registered Sale Deed in favour of A.Ramakrishna Shetty on 23.12.2003 and he was put in possession of the said property.
Hakku Pathra was also issued in his name.
His name has been entered in the revenue records.
On 01.02.2017, the said A.Ramakrishna Shetty executed a Registered Gift Deed in favour of his son R.K.Raghavendra in respect of the said property.
On 22.01.2021, said R.K.Raghavendra sold the written statement schedule property in favour of defendant No.2 for valuable sale consideration.
After purchase, the defendant No.2 is paying tax to the BBMP and get changed Khatha in his name.
B-Khatha was issued in the name of defendant No.2.
He is in possession and enjoyment of the written statement schedule property.
But there is no such suit schedule property in the said layout.
Without proper identification and existence of the suit schedule property, the plaintiff has filed this suit to knock off the property of defendant No.2.
The written statement schedule property was bounded on East by: Site No.2410; West and South by: Road and North by: Site No.2162.
Since the suit schedule property is not in existence, the plaintiff is not entitled for any relief and prayed for dismissal of the suit with exemplary cost.

4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the following issues have been framed for determination:-
ISSUES 1.
Whether the plaintiff proves his possession over the suit schedule property as on the date of the suit?
2. Whether the plaintiff proves the alleged interference caused by the defendants?
3. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to the relief of injunction?
4. What order or decree?

11. Placing reliance on the pleadings and evidence, the learned counsel for plaintiff has argued that,
as far as the right, title and interest of the plaintiff over the suit schedule property is not dispute.
The only contention taken by defendant No.2 is that, the suit schedule property is not in existence.

But the voluminous documents produced by the plaintiff makes it very clear that, the suit property is in existence and by virtue of the registered document, the plaintiff has acquired the valid right, title and interest over the suit schedule property.
Further argued that, as per Ex.P.8, the plaintiff herein had purchased the suit schedule property on 12.03.2020 for valuable consideration of Rs.60,00,000/-.

However, according to defendant No.2, he acquired right over the written statement schedule property by virtue of the Registered Sale Deed dated 22.01.2021 as per Ex.D.5,
for nominal sale consideration of Rs.15,00,000/-.

Even if the property of defendant No.2 is also situated in the very same layout, there are reasons to believe that, the market value of the property so purchased by defendant No.2 on subsequent date is much more than the value shown in the Sale Deed of plaintiff, marked at Ex.P.8.
That itself shows that, the defendant No.2 being a Land Grabber got the Sale Deed with an eagle eye to gulp down the property of plaintiff.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for plaintiff further canvassed before the court that, the documents relied by the plaintiff at Ex.P.16 and P.17 makes it very clear that, the site which was allotted in favour of A.Ramakrishna Shetty was acquired by the BDA for formation of road.
Further argued that, Ex.P.18 and P.19 were obtained by the plaintiff from the office of Karnataka State 'D' Group Employees Society under Right to Information Act.

The contents of those documents makes it clear that, the written statement schedule property was acquired for formation of layout and therefore, the original allottee A.Ramakrishna Shetty himself approached the Society with a request to pay compensation in respect of his site.
Further, he drew the attention of this court with respect to certain admissions made by defendant No.2 in the course of his cross- examination.
13. In his written arguments, the learned counsel for defendant No.2 has reiterated the contentions taken in the written statement.
14. In this background of the matter, I have carefully gone through the pleadings of the parties, their evidence, both oral and documentary.
The registered documents marked at Ex.P.2 and P.4 makes it very clear that, Smt.Savitha Muniraju, the vendor of plaintiff had acquired the suit schedule property.
Since there was minor mistake in the Sale Deed marked at Ex.P.2, the Rectification Deed was made as per Ex.P.4.
Now it is clear that, the description of the property and boundaries given in Ex.P.4 are tallies with plaint schedule.

Added to that, the other voluminous documents placed before the court makes it that, Smt.Savitha Muniraju, the vendor of plaintiff has acquired the absolute right, title and interest over the plaint schedule property and then Khatha came to be changed in her name and she being the absolute owner of the said property, alienated the same in favour of plaintiff and on the strength of Sale Deed, marked at Ex.P.8, he is the owner and in possession of the suit schedule property.
His ownership, right, title and interest over the suit schedule property was recognised by the concerned Authorities.
Accordingly, Khatha has been effected in his name and also power supply came to be changed in the name of plaintiff.

This being the factual position, it is crystal clear that, the preponderance of evidence is in favour of the plaintiff to hold that, as on the date of suit, he is in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.
15. Even though Ex.P.18 was marked subject to objections, this court cannot ignore the evidentiary value attached to Ex.P.18 and P.19.
The recitals of those documents give strong inference that, the property so purchased by A.Ramakrishna Shetty was acquired by the BDA for formation of road.
It also give an inference that, the defendant No.2 taking undue advantage of his Sale Deed, making an illegal attempt to interfere with the possession of plaintiff over the suit schedule property.

As rightly contended by the learned counsel for plaintiff, in his cross-examination dated 11.01.2024, the defendant No.2 has admitted that, the portion of property in the layout was acquired by the BDA for formation of road.
One more thing for consideration is that, the defendant did not produce the title deed of his vendor's vendor.
The explanation offered by him is that, the Sale Deed in favour of A.Ramakrishna Shetty was misplaced.
Admittedly, no any complaint was lodged in respect of misplacing of original Sale Deed.
It also give strong room to suspect about the bonafides of the defendant.

sentences.text: As stated supra, to prove his possession over the suit schedule property as on the date of suit, the plaintiff has produced the voluminous documents in his name, issued by the Competent Authorities.
Even if the suit schedule property is not in existence, there was no occasion to the concerned Authority to issue those documents in the name of plaintiff.

Further, the very denial of existence of suit schedule property by defendant No.2 makes it clear that, without having any right, title or interest over the suit schedule property, he is making an illegal attempt to interfere with the possession of the plaintiff.
Accordingly, Issues No.1 and 2 are answered in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:-

While answering the aforementioned issues, this court has come to the conclusion that, the plaintiff is in possession of the suit schedule property as on the date of suit and proved the interference caused by the defendant with respect to his possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule property.
In such circumstances, the plaintiff is entitled for an equitable relief of injunction.
Accordingly, Issue No.3 is answered in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.4:

In view of the above discussions, this court proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
Suit of the plaintiff is decreed as under;

The defendants No.1 and 2, their men, agents, servants or anybody claiming through them are hereby restrained from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the plaintiff over the suit schedule property.
No order as to cost.
Draw decree accordingly.
